x: Mitchell’s time was the 6th fastest for his stage, but his performance is better than would be thought at first glance, for among his rivals over this stretch were Beman, Harper, Holden of Tipton H.; Johnston, Herne Hill H ; Bignall, Highgate H.; and Oddie, S.L.H.; all of whom are “internationals.”

In the three miles Team Race at the Ravensbourne S.C meeting, Johnston, H.H.H., once again Belgrave, his first place negativing the good team-work of Penny, Footer and Mitchell, who all finished inside 15min. 20secs.

We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable).
Our boys got away to a good start and Black, Miller, Brown, Dabbs and Johnston were soon prominent, with Masters and Dooley further back but well positioned.

Ventor (98th) ran below form and Joe Dooley, although making considerable ground in the latter stages, could only reach 106th. The remaining finishers were Stearman (127), Johnston (136), Jones D.W. (139), Collier (146), and an unfit Sawyer (148).

Heck, Miller, Thresher, Moore and Johnston are but a few knocking on the door to 1st team honours. There are also those up-and-coming lads Cocks, Hampshire and Fairclough who will be dis-placing a few old-timers before long.
The Portsmouth team pointed out that they were without Tulloh and Johnston but would they have made over three minutes difference--I doubt it!!!
